purpose: A second runtime for a model the lab already serves through vLLM, on the same strict 12-prompt completions suite and the same metric, so the two are directly comparable.

model.note: The local copy came from an external drive and its digest matches this publisher revision exactly; the runner refuses to start otherwise.

runtime.flags: -ngl 99 -c 8192 -np 1 -b 1024 -ub 1024 -t 8 -fa on -ctk f16 -ctv f16 --reasoning off --ctx-checkpoints 0 --jinja, one B70 (SYCL0)
runtime.speculation: none: this GGUF carries no MTP head, so the comparison is against the vLLM no-speculation numbers

verdict: llama.cpp serves this model correctly and passes the workload gate, at 47.23 and 48.86 tok/s across two fresh servers. On the same card, suite and metric, vLLM with the same-size INT4 weights is 1.34x faster without speculation (64.33) and 2.36x faster with the model's own MTP head (113.63). First-token latency is about five times higher (247 ms against ~48 ms). The two fresh llama.cpp servers agreed on only 8 of 12 prompts, so this runtime is not repeat-exact here either: it is a third independent case, on a different runtime and a different quantization, of the tie-breaking variation that the lab's row-invariant INT4 kernel removes.
